name: AFTERLIFE ATLAS: Mortuary Worlds
description: An indie neural sim developed by a collective of Tier 1 and Tier 2 artists under the studio name Borrowed Light, AFTERLIFE ATLAS drops players into fully realized cultural afterlives drawn from dozens of blended global traditions — Yoruba-Shinto spirit forests, Andean-Norse mountain halls, Austronesian-Buddhist ocean depths. Each afterlife is a 40-60 hour experience designed to be played once, with no save states, forcing players to confront mortality as a design principle. The game sold 800,000 units in its first month entirely through pirate distribution before a legitimate release was brokered.
story_hooks: A grief-stricken parent plays AFTERLIFE ATLAS searching for their child in every cultural death-realm, convinced the game somehow contains something real.
Borrowed Light's lead designer goes missing after announcing a final, unreleased afterlife world — one built from their own neural architecture.
A corponation offers Borrowed Light an acquisition deal that would fund a sequel but require save states; the collective is fracturing over whether to accept.
